common_name: ColorBlaze Dark Star Coleus (Indigo-Purple Scalloped-Leaf Coleus)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; Dark Star, part of the ColorBlaze series, bears simple, mid-size, scalloped-edged leaves in an intensely dark indigo-purple that reads almost black, holding its color best with some direct morning sun.

directions: Plant in a spot that gets some morning sun with afternoon shade in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix; too much deep shade mutes the near-black color, causing the plant to fade into the background rather than standing out. Dark Star, part of the ColorBlaze series, bears simple, scalloped-edged leaves in an inky indigo-purple that ranks among the darkest foliage colors available in coleus, making it an outstanding foil for chartreuse, silver, or brightly colored companion plants in mixed beds and containers. Its steady, mounded habit and season-long color, extending from summer to the first hard frost, make it a reliable dark-foliage anchor for borders and large pots. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant's energy directed into foliage, and pinch growing tips periodically to encourage a fuller, bushier habit.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Finder — Solenostemon scutellarioides 'Dark Star'

common_name: Pink Chaos Coleus (Fiery Pink Dragon's-Tongue Variegated Coleus)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; Pink Chaos bears long, tapered, deeply toothed leaves boldly variegated in fiery pink, red, green, and white in an irregular, flame-like pattern often likened to a dragon's tongue.

directions: Plant in bright filtered light to partial shade, sheltered from harsh midday sun, in humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil or container mix. Pink Chaos bears narrow, tapered, deeply serrated leaves splashed in a chaotic, highly variegated pattern of hot pink, red, green, and cream, giving it a distinctive fine, flame-like texture unlike broad-leaved coleus cultivars. Its dense, upright habit and eye-catching foliage make it a standout in mixed containers or as a houseplant during the cooler months, since it also performs well indoors in bright indirect light. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to redirect energy into foliage, and pinch growing tips periodically to encourage a full, bushy habit; propagate by softwood cuttings, since named coleus cultivars do not come true from seed.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) Plants — Coleus scutellarioides 'Pink Chaos'

common_name: Kong Jr Scarlet Coleus (Compact Scarlet Yellow-Edged Shade Coleus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors or plant container plants after the last frost in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Kong Jr Scarlet is a compact-leaved companion to the large-leaved Kong series, with serrated, pointed scarlet leaves edged in lemon yellow.

directions: Plant in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, and keep soil consistently moist. Kong Jr Scarlet belongs to the Kong series bred for shade performance, but carries smaller, serrated, pointed leaves than the giant-leaved Kong originals, remaining bright scarlet edged with a distinctive lemon-yellow margin throughout the season on a vigorous, upright-spreading plant. Its bold color and finer-textured leaf make it a striking contrast plant for shaded beds, mixed containers, and hanging baskets, pairing well with ferns, hostas, and other shade perennials. Pinch flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant's energy directed into leaf growth, and pinch growing tips periodically to encourage a fuller, bushier habit.
sources: Ball Horticultural Company — Kong coleus series notes

common_name: Kong Jr Rose Coleus (Compact Lime-and-Rose Variegated Shade Coleus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors or plant container plants after the last frost in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Kong Jr Rose is a compact-leaved companion to the large-leaved Kong series, with lime-green leaves showily variegated in rose-pink and tinged dark red.

directions: Plant in moist, rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, and keep soil consistently moist. Kong Jr Rose belongs to the Kong series bred for shade performance, but carries smaller, serrated, pointed leaves than the giant-leaved Kong originals, staying lime green with showy rose-pink variegation and tinges of dark red throughout the season on a vigorous, upright-spreading plant. Its bright, finely textured foliage brings strong color to shaded beds, mixed containers, and hanging baskets, pairing well with ferns, hostas, and other big-leaved shade perennials. Pinch flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant's energy directed into leaf growth, and pinch growing tips periodically to encourage a fuller, bushier habit.
sources: Ball Horticultural Company — Kong coleus series notes

common_name: Under the Sea King Crab Coleus (Deeply-Cut Burgundy-and-Chartreuse Coleus)
scientific_name: Coleus scutellarioides 'Under the Sea King Crab'

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; King Crab, part of the Under the Sea series, bears large, deeply cut, pointed burgundy leaves edged in chartreuse with tinges of plum, the jagged lobes resembling crab pincers.

directions: Plant in partial shade to nearly full sun in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix. King Crab, part of the distinctively fine-textured Under the Sea coleus series, bears large, deeply cut, pointed burgundy leaves edged in bright chartreuse with tinges of plum-purple, the sharply lobed margins giving each leaf a crab-claw-like silhouette that sets it apart from the broad, solid leaves of typical coleus cultivars. Its upright-spreading habit and bold, dramatic foliage make it a strong textural accent in containers and mixed borders. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to redirect energy into fuller foliage, and pinch growing tips periodically to maintain a dense, bushy habit.
sources: Proven Winners — Under the Sea coleus series notes

common_name: Wizard Jade Coleus (Compact Cream-Centered Green-Edged Seed-Grown Coleus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors or plant after all frost danger has passed; Wizard Jade is a compact, seed-grown Wizard series coleus with creamy white leaf centers bordered by a sharp, medium-green margin, tolerant of both sun and shade.

directions: Plant in partial shade to nearly full sun in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix. Wizard Jade bears creamy white leaf centers bordered by a crisp, medium-green margin on a compact, uniform, seed-grown plant bred for reliable garden performance from a young age. Its bright, pale coloring lightens shaded beds and works well as filler in mixed containers or as edging along a walkway. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to redirect energy into fuller, more colorful foliage, and pinch growing tips periodically to maintain a dense, bushy habit.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Coleus as Annual Foliage Plant
Ball Horticultural Company — Wizard coleus series notes

common_name: Wizard Coral Sunrise Coleus (Compact Salmon-Pink Burgundy-Blotched Seed-Grown Coleus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors or plant after all frost danger has passed; Wizard Coral Sunrise is a compact, seed-grown Wizard series coleus with salmon-pink leaf centers marked with dark burgundy blotches and a medium-green margin, tolerant of both sun and shade.

directions: Plant in partial shade to nearly full sun in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix. Wizard Coral Sunrise bears salmon-pink leaf centers splashed with dark burgundy-brown blotches, more pronounced in fuller sun, and bordered by a medium-green margin on a compact, uniform, seed-grown plant bred for reliable garden performance from a young age. Its warm coral tones bring vibrant color to edging, mass bedding, and containers. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to redirect energy into fuller, more colorful foliage, and pinch growing tips periodically to maintain a dense, bushy habit.

common_name: Wizard Velvet Red Coleus (Compact Deep Burgundy-Red Seed-Grown Coleus)

planting.note: Start seed indoors or plant after all frost danger has passed; Wizard Velvet Red is a compact, seed-grown Wizard series coleus with velvety, bright burgundy-red leaves edged in a thin, pointed green margin, tolerant of both sun and shade.

directions: Plant in partial shade to nearly full sun in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix. Wizard Velvet Red bears velvety, deep burgundy-red leaves edged in a thin, pointed green margin on a compact, uniform, seed-grown plant bred for reliable garden performance from a young age. Its rich, saturated color makes it a strong companion to lime or chartreuse foliage in edging, mass bedding, and container plantings. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to redirect energy into fuller, more colorful foliage, and pinch growing tips periodically to maintain a dense, bushy habit.

common_name: Vino Coleus (Sun-Loving Deep Wine-Purple White-Edged Coleus)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; Vino bears deep, moody wine-purple leaves edged in white and is one of the few coleus cultivars whose color deepens rather than fades as sun exposure increases.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix; unlike most coleus, Vino intensifies from rich burgundy in shadier spots to an even deeper, more dramatic wine-purple in full sun, making it unusually versatile across light conditions. Its serrated, pointed leaves stay deep purple with a distinctive thin white edge, and its upright habit suits it well as a 'thriller' in mixed containers and hanging baskets or as a bold accent in the sunny border. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant's energy directed into foliage, and pinch growing tips periodically to encourage a full, dense, well-branched habit.
sources: Ball Horticultural Company — Vino coleus notes

common_name: Black Prince Coleus (Award of Garden Merit Near-Black Coleus)

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; Black Prince bears toothed, nearly solid purple-black leaves with a hint of red and is a recipient of the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its reliable garden performance.

directions: Plant in full sun to part shade in humus-rich, moist, well-drained soil or container mix. Black Prince bears toothed, softly ruffled leaves in a purple-black so dark it reads almost solid black, touched with a hint of red, among the darkest foliage colors available in coleus and an outstanding foil for chartreuse, silver, or brightly colored companion plants. It produces small spikes of lavender-and-white flowers in summer if left unpinched, and it has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for its heat tolerance and easy, low-maintenance garden performance. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to keep the plant's energy directed into foliage, and pinch growing tips periodically to encourage a full, dense, well-branched habit. Note: like other coleus, it is toxic to dogs, cats, and horses if ingested.
sources: Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) Plants — Solenostemon 'Black Prince'

common_name: Stained Glassworks Molten Lava Coleus (Orange Burgundy-Spined Shade Coleus)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Molten Lava, part of the Stained Glassworks series bred for deep shade, bears serrated oval leaves in bright orange with pointed burgundy spines and tinges of yellow.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; the Stained Glassworks series was bred specifically to hold strong foliage color and pattern in deeper shade than most coleus cultivars tolerate without fading or stretching. Molten Lava arose as a naturally occurring branch mutation of the cultivar Eclipse and bears serrated, oval leaves in fiery orange with pointed burgundy spines radiating from the veins and tinges of yellow, a striking, hot-colored departure from the purples and greens of most shade coleus. Its mounded habit and bright color make a bold accent in a shaded bed or large container. Pinch growing tips regularly to encourage a fuller, bushier habit and remove flower spikes as they form, since coleus declines in vigor once it sets seed.
sources: U.S. Plant Patent PP14426 — Coleus plant named 'Molten Lava'
